The problem

## Every new hire spends months finding out who knows what.

### You pay full salary from day one.

Real output starts months later, once they've found the pricing deck, learned why the last deal died and worked out which doc is current.

### You become the help desk.

Most questions land on you or a couple of senior people. Each answer is time you didn't spend on customers.

### Knowledge leaves with people.

Whatever sits in one person's head, or their private AI chat, walks out when they do.

How it works

## One company Brain. Any AI model.

Your business knowledge lives in plain files you own. Each job runs on whichever AI model does it best or cheapest, and every one reads the same Brain. Change models next year and you lose nothing.

### Your company Brain

Plain markdown in GitHub

-   `company-brain`everyone
-   `brain-<team>`department
-   `brain-<name>`private
-   `skills`shared library

### Grok agents

xAI's cloud

-   Daily brief
-   Daily check-in update
-   Meeting coordination

Fast, everyday assistant jobs

### Claude agents

Anthropic's cloud

-   Onboarding
-   Ask and Teach the Brain
-   Sales kit

Strong at following shared skills

### Open-weights agents

Your own server

-   Meeting notes capture
-   Weekly Brain digest

No per-use fees for high-volume jobs

Illustrative. We pick the models with you in week one. Agents can suggest additions to the Brain; a person approves them.

A new hire's first week

## What their first week looks like.

1.  Mon 9:00
    
    ### Setup takes an hour.
    
    One onboarding skill connects email, calendar, the Brain and a private password vault, then asks how they like to work.
    
2.  Mon 10:00
    
    ### Their agent already knows the company.
    
    What you sell, who buys it, how decisions get made. It never sees anyone's private notes, because it never gets access.
    
3.  Tue 7:30
    
    ### The brief is waiting.
    
    Every meeting with context, open promises and an agenda. Today it flags a timeline you promised a customer last week.
    
4.  Tue 9:00
    
    ### The daily update writes itself.
    
    Good news, top priority, what's stuck. Two minutes of answers and the team check-in is done.
    
5.  Tue 10:30
    
    ### Answers show their source.
    
    Ask what customers were told about data security and it shows the approved note. If nobody wrote it down, it says so and names who to ask.
    
6.  Week 2
    
    ### They add what they learn.
    
    A better answer to a pricing objection becomes a proposed page. Once approved, the next hire starts with it.
    

The package

## What you get.

We build it with you. You bring the knowledge and access to your tools. We bring the architecture, the AI skills and the training.

### Your company Brain

Your know-how in plain files you own, split by who's allowed to see what. Every change is logged and approved.

### Agents and skills

-   Onboarding, morning brief, daily update
-   Meeting notes captured once and filed
-   Ask the Brain, teach the Brain, weekly digest

### Reliability and guardrails

-   Each agent sees only what its person can see
-   Nothing leaves the company without a person
-   Broken connections flagged before the brief goes out

### Training

Your leaders go first. Then in-person workshops with the team, recorded and turned into self-serve onboarding every future hire follows alone.

1.  Week 1
    
    ### Design
    
    Pick the models, decide who sees what, name an owner for each part of the Brain.
    
2.  Weeks 2 to 5
    
    ### Build
    
    Brain, meeting capture, daily brief. Your leaders use it first.
    
3.  Weeks 6 to 7
    
    ### Train
    
    Recorded workshops with the team, then office hours.
    
4.  Week 8
    
    ### Hand over
    
    Self-serve onboarding, the Day-One Test, and an owner on your side.
    

1 hr

The Day-One Test

## How we know it works.

At hand-over, someone who has never seen the system sits down with only the self-serve package. Within an hour they're set up, and their agent correctly answers ten questions a new hire would normally ask a colleague.

-   No private content reaches someone who isn't allowed to see it
-   One record per meeting, however many people attended
-   When the Brain doesn't know, the agent says so instead of guessing

Who it's for

## Any company that hires faster than it can explain itself.

### Small business owners

You are the onboarding. Every new person learns the business from you, and little of it is written down. This gets it out of your head and into a Brain that trains the next hire for you.

### CEOs of growing companies

Each department has its own tools, docs and habits. One Brain with clear access rules gives every team the same answers and takes managers off help-desk duty.

### Startup founders

You're about to hire faster than you can onboard. Set the habit at ten people and it holds at a hundred, and investors see knowledge the company owns, with an audit trail.

What you'll need: one person who can connect your tools, a few hours a week from a leader for eight weeks, and your team's time for the workshops.
